provenance: All numbers and scenarios are original author-created hypothetical inputs, not observations, fitted estimates or real policy recommendations. No external dataset is embedded.

timing.availability: All scenario primitives are supplied before analysis. They are stipulated common knowledge within a deterministic scenario.
timing.decision: Regulator selects one instrument before firms choose outputs simultaneously. Consumers then buy at the market-clearing inverse-demand price.
timing.uncertainty_exercise: Regulator commits before the damage state is revealed. Firms know their unchanged private demand/costs; damage does not enter their private profit. Weights are supplied assumptions, not estimated frequencies.

units.demand_slope_quadratic_cost_damage_slope: USD per squared output unit in the fixed-period normalization

model.inverse_demand: P(Q) = A - b Q on the entire feasible output box; validated b*sum(capacities) <= A
model.cost: C_i(q_i) = c_i*q_i + k_i*q_i^2/2; no private fixed costs
model.damage: D(Q) = h*Q^2/2; one emission unit per output unit, no separate abatement margin
model.welfare: B(Q) - sum(C_i) - D(Q) - real administration, with B(Q)=A*Q-b*Q^2/2
model.competition: Price-taking benchmark using the same two production technologies; not a claim that two real firms ignore market power.
model.cournot: Two independent quantity setters; fixed participants; no entry, collusion, uncertainty about private primitives or repeated-game incentives.
model.standard: Equal nontradable firm upper bounds q_i <= min(physical_capacity_i,s); free allocation; no permit trading or permit auction revenue.
model.tax: Uniform nonnegative unit charge t in [0,tax_ceiling]; no subsidy; transfers have no additional collection/financing distortion beyond stated administration.
model.administration: A deployed tax or standard incurs its fixed real cost even if it has no output effect. A separately specified no-policy option incurs zero administration.
model.budget: Government net cash equals tax receipts minus administration. A negative balance is financed by an available lump-sum public numeraire endowment; positive balances are retained or rebated lump sum. The real administration cost is counted once.
model.preferences: Quasilinear dollar benefits, no binding income or financing constraint, unweighted total surplus including affected outsiders. This is an efficiency criterion, not a distributional ethical ranking.

protocol.policy_tie_rule: Maximize exact net welfare; then prefer no policy, then tax, then standard. Within equal tax welfare choose lower t; within equal standard welfare choose larger s.
protocol.stress_test: Carry baseline Cournot tax 16 and standard 16 unchanged into every deterministic scenario; also report scenario-specific optimized policies separately.
protocol.chart: Baseline Cournot net welfare versus tax t from 0 to 40 in steps of 1; deployed-tax cost applies at t=0 too. Plot no-policy welfare as a distinct labeled reference.

scenarios.label: Second firm too costly to operate

damage_uncertainty.assumption: Only h differs across these states. A single fixed instrument is selected ex ante; it cannot be changed after observing h.
